title: Geotechnical report review checklist
status_note: First draft, written by the lead from the 2026-10-06 field session and set down in module_work/SCALES_COVERAGE_CROSSCHECKS.md (W4 b) for the owner to mark up. Not yet approved: add, cut or reword items, and say which [judge] items code should learn to check.
how_it_is_used: One file, used two ways. Items with mode 'code' are checked by the app (funhouse_agent/report_checklist.py) from its own records: the coverage ledger of what was read, the text layer of the report, and the cross-checks subsurface.write_diggs runs on the data it is given. Items with mode 'judge' are handed to the agent by the report_checklist tool, to work through and report against. A 'code' item whose check cannot run in a conversation (for example no data has been written yet) goes to the agent as a judgement item, so nothing on the list is silently dropped.
how_to_edit: Edit the 'text' of an item freely. 'mode' is 'code' or 'judge'. A 'code' item names its 'check' (one of the checks in funhouse_agent/report_checklist.py: logs_and_lab_read, explorations_vs_logs, lab_ids_vs_logs, summary_and_sheets, cross_checks, values_cite_pages) and may narrow cross_checks with 'kinds' (the reconciler's: conflict, disagreement, partial, unconverted, count_mismatch) or 'where'. Keep the 'id' of an item that stays, so results can be compared between versions.

items.text: Every exploration named in the text, on the location plan or in a boring list has a log in the report, and every log names an exploration that is listed.
Every log page and every lab sheet was read, stated as counts.
Every sample on a lab summary table has a sheet, and every sheet is on the summary.
Every campaign is identified and dated: earlier reports bound in, and the newest borings.
Groundwater is recorded for every boring, or stated as not encountered.
Locations, elevations and their datum are stated.
Summary-table values match the individual sheets (the reconciler).
Lab sample IDs and depths match samples on the logs.
Log descriptions agree with the lab classification of the same sample.
Groundwater and stratigraphy stated in the text agree with the logs.
Which campaign governs, and whether superseded data are used in the recommendations.
The code editions cited (seismic code, ASCE 7 edition) are current for the project.
Every extracted value cites its page.
Every recommendation traces to data in the report.
Values are plausible for the soil described: N against the density description, moisture against classification.
Design parameters derived from the data, with the method cited.
Topics the data call for are addressed: bearing, settlement, seismic site class, liquefaction, and corrosion or chemistry exposure for concrete and steel.
